## Reporting a bug

<!--

Before submitting a bug report please ensure that you can check off these boxes:

-->

- [x] I have tried using the latest released version of Numba (most recent is
 visible in the change log (https://github.com/numba/numba/blob/main/CHANGE_LOG).
- [X] I have included a self contained code sample to reproduce the problem.
  i.e. it's possible to run as 'python bug.py'.

It seems it is impossible to call a `generated_jit`-decorated function from inside a CUDA kernel. Example below.

I am in the process of making a CPU-numba library dual use. Unfortunately, some simple `generated_jit` routines are used in a number of different places in CPU jit-compiled code. Workarounds that iron out the resulting problems without having to duplicate code would be much appreciated. (Or a fix of this issue, of course!)

```py
"""
Test CUDA kernel call to @generated_jit function.
"""
from typing import Union, Any, TypeVar, Type
import numpy as np
import numba as nb  # type: ignore
from numba import cuda  # type: ignore
from ingolstadt.util import mathutil


def test_cuda_generated_jit() -> None:
    """
    Test CUDA kernel call to @generated_jit function.
    """
    generated_jit_kernel[1, 1]()  # type: ignore


T = TypeVar("T", float, np.floating[Any])


@nb.generated_jit  # type: ignore
def nan_of_type(f: T) -> T:
    ff: Type[T] = f  # type: ignore
    if ff is np.float32:
        return lambda f: np.float32(np.nan)  # type: ignore
    elif ff is np.float64:
        return lambda f: np.float64(np.nan)  # type: ignore
    else:
        raise NotImplementedError(f"Unsupported type")


@cuda.jit  # type: ignore
def generated_jit_kernel() -> None:
    f = np.float32(2.0)
    n = nan_of_type(f)
    print("Nan", n)
```
title: Error when calling `nb.generated_jit` from CUDA
